deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen surfaces a modest but meaningful value pocket: 20 Strong Buys and 46 Buys against 142 Holds and 41 Avoids, so actionable ideas exist but remain a minority of the universe. The five highest-ranked names cluster in Industrials (FirstGroup, ME Group, Grafton) with one Healthcare (Hikma) and one Communication Services (ITV) name, suggesting cyclical and operational businesses rather than deep financials or tech. All top candidates pass across all five model families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) with full data quality (20/20 metrics), yet conviction scores are low (39–53%) and every name is flagged as a new, one-week signal. A key caution: several top picks carry FCF and earnings-basis overlays that downgrade the headline Strong Buy to Buy, and filing-aligned versus screen TTM versus company-adjusted cash flows diverge materially — valuation and yield screens may be overstating sustainability until those definitions are reconciled.

FGP.L (FirstGroup plc) — Industrials. Ten of 22 models pass (composite 91%, sector-relative 86%), led by Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality; key metrics are P/E 9.1, P/B 1.4, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%. Failures centre on leverage (D/E 161%), weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73), thin margins, and FCF Yield suppression due to a filing ($362.6M) vs screen TTM ($302.8M) vs company-adjusted (£73.8M) mismatch; statutory earnings growth is −5.9%. With two other Industrials in the top five, sector concentration is a consideration. Verdict: watchlist — cheap on earnings and contrarian ranks, but leverage, liquidity, and unresolved FCF basis noise warrant confirmation before sizing.

HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC) — Healthcare. Ten of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%), including Graham Enterprising, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Composite Value, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 12.7, P/B 1.9, yield 3.8%, ROE 15.4%, D/E 77%. Fails include FCF Yield (3.5% vs 5% threshold), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and a healthcare price-erosion overlay; FCF filing ($119M) vs screen TTM ($14.4M) diverges sharply, and net FCF/dividend coverage is 0.64×. Verdict: watchlist — sector-relative cheapness and quality screens are supportive, but cash conversion and US generic pricing pressure need manual diligence.

MEGP.L (ME Group International plc) — Industrials. Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 83%, sector-relative 88%) — the broadest pass rate in the group — including Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 7.9, P/B 2.3, yield 7.1%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%. An interim-quality overlay flags declining interim EPS and net FCF/dividend coverage below 1.0× (0.84× net); Piotroski F-Score is 6/9 and Earnings Quality fails on weak free-cash conversion. Third Industrials name in the top five. Verdict: accumulate — deepest model support and strong moat metrics, but size for dividend sustainability given sub-1× net FCF coverage.

ITV.L (ITV plc) — Communication Services. Fourteen of 22 models pass (composite 78%, sector-relative 88%), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (PEG 0.45, growth 26.7%), High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, and Earnings Quality; metrics are P/E 11.9, P/B 1.6, yield 7.0%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%. Piotroski F-Score is a weak 3/9 (ROA, leverage, and margin trends all failing), and FCF filing ($148M) vs screen TTM ($211.9M) vs company-adjusted (£325M) diverges; timing signal is "accumulate" with RSI 40 and price below the 200-day MA. Verdict: accumulate — favourable entry timing and strong income/value screens, but structural media decline and weak F-Score argue for staged entry.

GFTU.L (Grafton Group plc) — Industrials. Eleven of 22 models pass (composite 83%, sector-relative 80%), notably Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, Schloss Low P/B, FCF Yield (9.3%), Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 12.6, P/B 1.2, yield 3.7%, ROE 8.4%, D/E 38%, current ratio 2.11, with net FCF/dividend coverage 2.83×. Failures reflect modest ROE (8.4%), thin margins, Lynch PEG (1.50), and no deep-value or moat confirmation; no FCF basis overlay and the only top pick retaining adjusted_signal "strong_buy". Fourth Industrials name. Verdict: accumulate — cleanest balance sheet and cash coverage in the group, with Graham-style defensiveness offsetting cyclical exposure.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 161%) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73) are not fully captured by passing value screens; open question on pension/OPEB obligations and UK transport regulatory/franchise renewal risk.
- FGP.L: Statutory earnings growth −5.9% vs adjusted EPS growth +16% — governance and accounting policy choices around adjusted metrics need review.
- HIK.L: Healthcare price-erosion overlay signals filing-level pricing pressure not reflected in headline yield screens; open question on US FDA/competitive generic erosion and pipeline concentration.
- HIK.L: Net FCF/dividend coverage 0.64× and screen TTM FCF ($14.4M) vs filing ($119M) — dividend sustainability and capex cycle risk are open questions.
- MEGP.L: Interim EPS decline and net FCF/dividend coverage 0.84× suggest the 7.1% yield may be cyclically inflated; open question on photo-booth/kiosk discretionary spend sensitivity and geographic revenue mix.
- MEGP.L: P/B 2.3 fails deep-value criteria — asset-light model may mask lease-adjusted leverage not in D/E ratio.
- ITV.L: Piotroski F-Score 3/9 indicates deteriorating operating trends (OCF < net income, rising leverage, margin compression); open question on structural advertising share loss to streaming and content spend escalation.
- ITV.L: 7.0% yield with net FCF/dividend coverage 0.79× — dividend cut risk in a cyclical ad downturn is not scored by income screens.
- GFTU.L: Low ROE (8.4%) and building-materials cyclicality — housing/construction downturn exposure is not explicitly modelled despite strong current financial health scores.
- GFTU.L: Open question on M&A integration risk and cross-border (UK/Ireland/Netherlands) regulatory exposure given the distribution-heavy business model.

documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary: FirstGroup is a UK-focused bus and rail operator that has reshaped itself since exiting North America, combining a recovering earnings base with active capital returns. The quantitative screen rates the stock a **strong buy** (composite 91%, 10/22 models; P/E 9.1, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%, Piotroski 8/9), supported by cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP and risk families. Filings show adjusted EPS rising from 19.4p (FY 2025) to 20.3p (FY 2026), with a £100m buyback launched in June 2026 and total dividend of 7.2p, but adjusted net debt has risen to £137.7m amid heavy bus electrification capex. The central debate is whether open-access rail growth, London bus scale and DfT TOC wind-down cash (~£125m over three years) outweigh bus volume pressure (underlying commercial volumes −7% in H1), rail nationalisation and noisy free-cash-flow definitions that the screen itself flags.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, the case rests on **statutory-quality cash generation at a modest multiple**, not deep net-net territory. The screen passes earnings yield (E/P ~11%), low P/E plus yield, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), composite value and earnings quality — a breadth unusual for a cyclical transport name. Business quality is better than the leverage-heavy balance sheet suggests at first glance: management fee-based DfT train operations carry minimal commercial risk, open access (Lumo, Hull Trains) is growing (open access revenue £109.3m in FY 2026 per the annual report highlights), and First Bus London plus bolt-on coach acquisitions diversify revenue away from pure regional commercial bus.

Capital allocation aligns with value: progressive dividends (~3× adjusted EPS cover, tightening toward 2.5×), completed £50m buyback (H1 FY 2026), a further **£100m programme** announced at FY 2026 results (18 June 2026), and surplus-cash return policy. FY 2026 adjusted net debt of £137.7m remains within the stated medium-term target of below 2.0× adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA. The screen’s strong-buy signal is tempered by overlays on **FCF basis mismatch** (filing-aligned $362.6m vs company-adjusted £73.8m vs screen TTM $302.8m) and **statutory vs adjusted EPS growth divergence** — both noted in `screening_snapshot.json` — so the value case is real but not clean on cash-yield screens (FCF Yield model failed).

Bus franchising pipeline (~**£1bn** revenues over five years) and **£3 fare cap** pressure (commercial volumes **−6%** FY 2026).
- **Accounting/governance (partially de-risked):** FY 2026 **zero adjusting items**; statutory/adjusted operating profit aligned. Adjusted policy excludes IFRS 16 on DfT TOC leases — disclosed and consistent, not hidden reserve release. Prior-year **£167.6m** DfT levy reclassification affects revenue comparatives only.

- **Pension:** Net surplus **£19.9m** at FY 2026 year-end (improved from H1 deficit); **~£65m** escrow pending 2030 valuations — improved vs interim but not fully closed out.
- **Competitive:** ORR rejected Hull Trains Sheffield route; open-access growth requires regulatory approval for **~£1bn** seat-mile applications.
- **Going concern:** Confirmed to **30 September 2027** in FY 2026 results RNS; no material uncertainty stated in available extracts.

Statutory basic EPS is **21.4p** (FY 2025: **21.3p**, +0.5%); adjusted EPS is **20.3p** (FY 2025: **19.4p**, +4.6%). Adjusted metrics exclude IFRS 16 depreciation/interest on DfT TOC rolling-stock leases (£2.8m adjustment in FY 2026) because the Group bears no cost risk on those leases; FY 2025 comparatives included discontinued-operation adjusting items (legacy Greyhound US pension buy-out gain **£5.1m**). The H1 interim (`ir_032b08900a650e14.txt`) documents adjusting-item policy: items below **£5m** are normally excluded unless part of a strategic project. The screen’s **−5.9% statutory earnings growth** aligns with Yahoo net income ($118.3m vs $127.5m) in `financials_annual.json`, not filing EPS — a source mismatch, not evidence of current earnings manipulation.

Company policy uses **adjusted net debt £137.7m** (target **<2.0×** adjusted net debt to Rail-adjusted EBITDA; EBITDA **£231.9m** → **~0.6×**), with **£364.1m** undrawn committed facilities and going concern to September 2027. documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary:
Hikma Pharmaceuticals is a FTSE 100 multinational generic and branded medicines group with three divisions — Injectables, Branded (MENA) and Hikma Rx (US oral/specialty) — reporting in US dollars and generating roughly 58% of H1 2026 revenue from the United States. The quantitative screen rates the name a **Strong Buy** on cheapness (P/E 12.7, P/B 1.9), a 3.8% dividend yield, 15.4% ROE and broad model passes across quality, dividend, GARP and risk families, albeit with screen overlays on healthcare pricing pressure, earnings-basis divergence and FCF inconsistency. The valuation hook is a depressed multiple after a February 2026 guidance reset and share-price fall, partially reversed by a solid H1 2026 profit beat and a $250 million buyback. The central debate is whether Branded and Hikma Rx momentum, capital return and US manufacturing scale can offset Injectables margin compression, elevated capex and statutory earnings that are flattish once legal settlements are stripped out.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Hikma offers a rare combination of **sector-defensive cash generation**, **investment-grade balance sheet** (BBB/stable at S&P and Fitch) and **multiple valuation anchors** that align with the screen’s Strong Buy signal.

**Quantitative alignment.** Ten of 22 models pass, spanning Graham Enterprising, Neff PEGY, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value and Financial Health. Key metrics — P/E 12.7, P/B 1.92, yield 3.8%, debt/equity 77%, current ratio 1.8 — sit comfortably within value thresholds. The screen passes five factor families (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) with full data quality (20/20 metrics). Failures are instructive rather than disqualifying: FCF Yield, Lynch PEG and Economic Moat fail on FCF conversion, negative statutory earnings growth and sub-moat ROE (15.4% vs 18% hurdle), consistent with a cyclical/generic pricing backdrop rather than a broken balance sheet.

**Business quality.** Primary filings show a structurally improving mix: Branded delivered 15% H1 2026 revenue growth and 32.5% core operating margin; Hikma Rx core operating margin expanded to 20.6% in H1 2026 from 17.3% in FY2025. The Group is the largest pharma company by sales in MENA and a top-three US injectables supplier by volume. FY2025 core operating profit of $741 million (+3%) on revenue of $3,349 million (+6% core, constant currency) demonstrates underlying earnings power despite Injectables headwinds.

**Capital allocation.** Management increased the total dividend 5% to 84 cents for FY2025 and launched a $250 million buyback in February 2026; by 5 August 2026, $227 million had been executed. ROIC was 16.0% at FY2025 (filing). These actions support the screen’s dividend and quality passes while the share price trades below broker re-rating levels post-H1.

**Why Strong Buy, not deep value.** The name is not a net-net or deep P/B play (P/B 1.9; Graham Defensive and Schloss fail). It is a **quality-at-a-reasonable-price** generic pharma compounder with a geographic and segment hedge — Branded growth funding Injectables reinvestment — that the screen correctly identifies at a sector-relative composite of 91%.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary:
ME Group International operates ~49,000 self-service vending units across 16 countries, chiefly photobooths (Photo.ME) and unattended laundry (Wash.ME). FY2025 (year ended 31 October 2025) delivered record profit before tax of £78.2m on revenue of £315.4m, with laundry now contributing 46% of group EBITDA. The quantitative screen flags deep value on P/E ~7.9×, P/B ~2.3×, dividend yield ~7.1%, ROE ~28%, and modest leverage (debt/equity ~28%), supported by net cash of £26.5m at year-end.

The valuation hook is a cash-generative, asset-heavy franchise trading below earnings power while pivoting mix toward higher-return laundry installations (ASDA, SNCF, RATP renewals). The central debate is whether photobooth regulatory disruption (Germany passport rules, Japan ID changes), April 2026 consumer softness in France, and repeated accounting restatements are cyclical/transitory—or structural impairments to a business the market prices as permanently cheap. H1 FY2026 profit before tax fell 3.8% to £32.7m; management now guides FY2026 PBT to £69–74m, below the FY2025 record.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MEGP combines classic cheapness with identifiable business quality. The screen passes five factor families—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with 20/20 data completeness. Trailing metrics (P/E 7.9, earnings yield ~12.6%, FCF yield on filing-aligned £25.2m free cash flow) sit well below sector norms, while ROE of 28.2% and net cash position argue against a distressed balance sheet.

Business quality rests on durable site-owner relationships (no customer >2% of turnover), high-footfall locations, and a proven diversification playbook: Wash.ME vending revenue grew 10.2% in FY2025 and 16.3% in H1 FY2026, with EBITDA margins above 50%. Capital is reinvested at attractive paybacks—FY2025 capex was £65.6m, cash from operations £115.5m—and management returned £32.6m via dividends plus launched an £18m buyback (3.6m shares repurchased for £4.5m by end-July 2026).

The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a compounder-in-transition narrative: photobooth cash flows fund laundry roll-out, mix shift improves group EBITDA margin (38.2% FY2025; 36.9% H1 FY2026 despite softer top line). Failed models (Graham Defensive, net-net, Piotroski 6/9, earnings quality) correctly flag that this is not a balance-sheet bargain or pristine accruals story—interim EPS declined, net FCF/dividend coverage is 0.84× per screen overlay, and photobooth headwinds are real. The adjusted screen signal (Buy after interim-quality overlay) is more appropriate than blind strong-buy: value is present, but earnings durability requires verification.

---
documents.financial_review:
*Primary source: RNS annual and interim body extracts; IR presentation bridge and screen metrics where noted.*

FY2025 delivered record PBT £78.2m on revenue £315.4m, with filing-aligned FCF £25.2m and dividends paid £29.8m (net coverage 0.84×, gross 1.68×). The balance sheet is asset-heavy (PPE £169.5m), not asset-light: net cash £26.5m excludes £13.0m lease liabilities; total borrowings and leases £43.0m (~20% of equity). Geographic concentration: Continental Europe 68.3% of FY2025 revenue, 67.1% of H1 FY2026.

H1 FY2026 shows the cyclical/demand inflection in numbers: PBT −3.8%, implied H1 FCF ~£4.8m (OCF £38.7m less capex £33.9m) vs £14.5m dividends paid (~0.33× coverage). Management responded by cutting the interim dividend 6.5% to 3.60p while maintaining the £18m buyback and laundry capex programme. April 2026 data split Photo.ME −17% vs Wash.ME +3%, supporting the view that yield risk sits in photobooth/kiosk cyclicality rather than laundry growth.

FY2026 PBT guided £69–74m (June trading update). Remaining gaps: no FY2026 final dividend proposal; H1 monthly France series not in local pack.

---
documents.risks_and_flags:
**Evidenced:** German/Japan ID regulation (Photo.ME); April France cyclical trough; FY2025 net FCF/dividend gap with interim dividend cut as partial mitigation; lease liabilities £13.0m excluded from net-cash headline; accounting restatements (cash-in-transit, dividend timing); governance events (audit delay, Montefiore secondary placing at 132p, strategic review termination); net cash declining to £7.5m but still positive.

**Still open:** Germany revenue recovery post next-gen booth rollout (needs H2 FY2026 trading updates); IFRS 16 lease maturity profile (note 20 referenced but not extracted); FY2026 final dividend level after guidance cut.

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run surfaced 66 buy-tier names (20 Strong Buy, 46 Buy) from 249 screened, but conviction on the top five remains capped at 39–53% and every name is a new one-week signal. The dominant systemic weakness is not missing filings at index time—buy-tier `indexed_without_body` is 0 across all 20 tickers—but a scoring-metadata layer that still feeds models stale or empty Yahoo TTM cash flows while filing-aligned figures diverge by an order of magnitude (e.g. HIK.L screen TTM FCF $14.4M vs filing $119M). Gap-fill materially improved FGP.L, HIK.L, and MEGP.L memo grades to “strong” with source quality 0.885–1.0, yet HIK.L’s three open questions stay only partially resolved and FGP.L/HIK.L deep-analysis verdicts remain watchlist-grade on leverage, FCF basis, and dividend coverage. FCF and earnings-basis overlays are downgrading headline Strong Buys to Buy across the cohort, so top picks are researchable but not yet conviction-ready without reconciling cash-flow definitions and fixing TTM ingest.
post_run_review.persistent_weaknesses:
- **Ingest — indexed filings without extractable bodies** (backlog area leader: 115 of 259 suggestions, ~44%): Recurring pattern to pull Investegate/LSE RNS HTML or PDF bodies instead of Google News wrappers; backlog samples cite AEP.L with 31 indexed filings and `with_body: 0`, and MEGP.L with 52 indexed / 0 bodies before this run’s refetch. This week’s gap-fill fetched +30 bodies for FGP.L and +29 for MEGP.L via the same pipeline.
- **Ingest — IR allowlist PDF extraction failures** (HIK.L, MEGP.L, GFTU.L, ITV.L in backlog high-priority samples): Direct company-IR PDFs (results presentations, trading updates, annual reports) repeatedly fail or return wrong documents; `ir_presentation_metrics.json` left at `bridge_count: 0` for FGP.L until manual RNS read.
- **Ingest — mis-attributed / duplicate refetch bodies** (HIK.L this run; backlog ingest theme): Investegate HTML fallback ingested H1 interim text under April 2026 trading-update URL (`ir_a9733d0de6aec27d`); content-hash dedup not enforced.
- **Ingest — Yahoo quarterly cashflow gaps block TTM metrics** (HIK.L; recurring in recent suggestions): Empty `quarterly_cashflow` in `financials_annual.json` produces unreconcilable screen TTM FCF; also MEGP.L backlog item for missing `operating_cashflow` in `CompanyMetrics` despite £90.8M in annual JSON.
- **Scoring — three-way FCF definition mismatch** (63 backlog suggestions, 29 in recent 111): Filing-aligned vs screen TTM vs company-adjusted figures diverge on FGP.L ($362.6M / $302.8M / £73.8M), ITV.L ($148M / $211.9M / £325M), HIK.L ($119M / $14.4M), triggering false FCF Yield and Earnings Quality failures and Strong Buy → Buy downgrades.
- **Scoring — earnings-basis / adjusted-vs-statutory growth mismatch** (FGP.L this run; backlog theme): Yahoo statutory earnings growth −5.9% contradicts filing EPS 21.4p vs 21.3p and triggers false earnings-basis overlay.

rules: Universe: only strong_buy / buy names from the latest screen.
Timing filter: names with timing_signal=wait are excluded from new buys.
Sector cap: at most 1 name(s) per known sector (cap=20%).
Ranking: highest conviction_score first, keep at most 3 names.
Sizing: equal-weight sleeves of current NAV after exits; buys limited by remaining cash.
Costs: 3.0% applied on each buy and sell.
Hold buffer: full exit only after 2 consecutive rebalance(s) outside the target set.
Re-entry cooldown: wait 1 rebalance(s) after a full exit before buying the same name again.
Dust guard: skip trim/top-up adjustments below £10.
plan.summary: Next rebalance would target 3 equal-weight sleeve(s); leave 1 near-target holding(s).
